# invoice-export

Turns the invoices of the billing system into the CSV file the accounting team imports every month.

## Usage

```
npm run export > invoices.csv
```

This runs `node src/cli.js data`: it reads `invoices.json`, `billing-customers.json` and `crm-customers.json` from
the given directory (default `data/`) and prints one CSV row per invoice, in the order of `invoices.json`.

The customers come from two systems. `billing-customers.json` is exported by the billing system, and
`crm-customers.json` holds the customers that were created in the CRM. Both are read as they are delivered. The
accounting import expects the CSV columns `invoice_id,customer,issued_on,total`, so the format must not change.

## Tests

```
npm test
```

Plain `node --test`, no dependencies. Tests live in `tests/`.

## Conventions

- Money is handled in integer cents and formatted only at the edge (`src/money.js`).
- A reference to something that does not exist, such as an unknown customer, is a data error. It is reported with
  `UnknownReferenceError` naming what was not found (see `requireCustomer`), and the CLI then exits with status 1
  and prints nothing to stdout. The export never skips a record or prints a placeholder for it: a file with a
  missing invoice is worse for accounting than no file.

# invoice-export

Turns the invoices of the billing system into the CSV file the accounting team imports every month.

## Usage

```
npm run export > invoices.csv
```

This runs `node src/cli.js data`: it reads `invoices.json`, `billing-customers.json` and `crm-customers.json` from
the given directory (default `data/`) and prints one CSV row per invoice, in the order of `invoices.json`.

The customers come from two systems. `billing-customers.json` is exported by the billing system, and
`crm-customers.json` holds the customers that were created in the CRM. Both are read as they are delivered. The
accounting import expects the CSV columns `invoice_id,customer,issued_on,total`, so the format must not change.

## Tests

```
npm test
```

Plain `node --test`, no dependencies. Tests live in `tests/`.

## Conventions

- Money is handled in integer cents and formatted only at the edge (`src/money.js`).
- A reference to something that does not exist, such as an unknown customer, is a data error. It is reported with

  and prints nothing to stdout. The export never skips a record or prints a placeholder for it: a file with a
  missing invoice is worse for accounting than no file.

content.text:
`npm run export` now runs to the end and prints all eight invoices, including INV-1041 (Birch & Co). All 13 tests pass, including the two new ones. I haven't committed anything.

**Cause:** The CRM export (`crm-customers.json`) calls the id field `customer_id`. The billing export and the rest of the code use `customerId`. Every CRM customer (C-2201, C-2202, C-2203) was therefore indexed under `undefined`. Any invoice for one of them found no customer, which gave the `undefined.name` crash.

**Changes:**
- `src/sources.js`: CRM records are now converted to `customerId` when they're loaded.
- `src/export.js`: a missing customer now goes through `requireCustomer`. It raises the documented `UnknownReferenceError` (e.g. `Unknown customer "C-9" (referenced by invoice INV-9)`) and exits 1 with nothing on stdout. Before, it was a raw `TypeError`. Real missing customers still stop the export, as the README requires.
- Tests: one for loading CRM customers (`tests/sources.test.js`) and one for the unknown-customer error (`tests/export.test.js`).

The CSV columns and format are the same as before. To produce the file for accounting, run `npm run export > invoices.csv`.
